summary: ```markdown # What are the Precautions for Importing Virtual Models? ## How to Add Arrangement Points and Arrangement Boards? ### Introduction In this video, we will learn about the knowledge of the arrangement point and arrangement board. ### Importing a Virtual Model First of all, when we import a virtual model, if it is an OBJ file, it will automatically generate an arrangement board upon import. Whether it is imported from the file folder or from the upper left corner, the process is the same. Here, confirm the type of download, the type of object, and confirm the unit at the bottom. A pop-up window may appear to remind you that you cannot arrange the arrangement point on the virtual model. There are several possibilities for this pop-up window to appear: 1. Your posture makes the system unable to identify a more accurate A or T pose. 2. Your model may have a more special shape. 3. Your proportion unit has some issues. The proportion unit is relatively easy to solve—just import the correct unit and pay attention to it. ### Checking the Arrangement Points Here, I import a virtual model with a posture that is the standard A pose. After this model is imported, we can press Shift + F to see if there is an arrangement point or select the display arrangement point in the vertical guide list. You will see that an automatic arrangement point is generated. This occurs because our current action is an A pose, which is easier for the system to identify. When importing a virtual model, it is best not to raise your arms too high. Click on the board and then click on the arrangement point to arrange the board around the virtual model. ### Editing Arrangement Boards and Points If we want to change the arrangement board or arrangement point, or if we want to create a new arrangement board or arrangement point, we can go to the main menu and find the Virtual Model Editor. There is a virtual model editor located at the bottom of the virtual model main menu. After opening it, we find the arrangement point. As we locate the arrangement point, the green arrangement board and the blue arrangement point will be displayed in the 3D space. When we arrange a board on the arrangement point, it will be placed along the shape of the green arrangement board. Whether we click on the name at the bottom of the arrangement board or the name at the bottom of the arrangement point, the corresponding objects will be highlighted in yellow. If the name has a lowercase 'a' or 'l' at the back, this indicates that they are symmetrical. ### Creating Symmetrical Boards If I create a board and press Ctrl + D, I can create a symmetrical board. In this way, whether editing or creating a sewing line, they are linked. If I arrange one of the boards on the arrangement point, the other board will also be automatically arranged on the symmetrical arrangement point. When editing or creating an arrangement board or arrangement point, we can apply such rules. ### Saving Arrangement Boards and Points Back in the Virtual Model Editor, to quickly use these arrangement boards and arrangement points, we can choose to save them. Please note that in general, arrangement points and arrangement boards will have a corresponding principle. Therefore, if you save the arrangement board, you must also remember to save the arrangement points. This way, we can use these arrangement boards and points in another position or another virtual model. ### Creating an Arrangement Board Next, let's learn how to create an arrangement board. Press the plus button on the arrangement board to create a new board. After creating it, click and drag this arrangement board to move it. When selecting an arrangement board, its corresponding properties will appear at the bottom of the arrangement editor. Here, we can modify the length of the entire arrangement board, as well as its height in the x and y dimensions. The heights in x and y are modified based on the coordinate system of the arrangement board itself and can differ from each other. ### Using Positioning Balls Click the arrangement board again to call for a positioning ball. By using the positioning ball, we can rotate the arrangement board to the correct angle. Additionally, we can switch the arrangement type in the arrangement property. Here, we can choose a cylinder-type arrangement or a cuboid, which is a rectangular shape. If you select Cuboid, when the board is arranged outside the rectangular shape, it will automatically be arranged into a foldable shape. Under normal circumstances, we choose Cylinder. ### Creating a Layout After creating a layout, we need to create a layout under this arrangement board. First, click "Add" to create a new layout. After creating a layout, we find the PAN that we created before. This newly created layout board will have the layout point placed on it. However, if we adjust or modify the name later, we may need to manually arrange the board in the layout point again. As we rotate the rectangle in 3D, you will see that the layout point has been placed on the layout board. We can adjust the location of the layout point through x and y, where x is the horizontal position and y is the vertical axis. ### Direction of the Package When the layout point is placed on the layout board, this point will lean outward. The direction of the package is significant: if the direction of the package is down, the board will rotate from the outside to the inside according to the vertical axis. Conversely, if the direction is up, the axis will rotate accordingly. ### Creating a Symmetrical Layout Board To create a symmetrical layout board, first build the initial layout board and set it to the same value as the previous layout board. The name of the new layout board must correspond to the previous layout board, with a lower line and a capital 'R' added, and for the original, a lower line and a capital 'L'. Next, we set the value of this new layout board to mirror the previous one. We then manually arrange it using the positioning ball tool. If your positioning ball differs from mine, you can right-click it in 3D space and select "World Coordinate." This makes it more convenient to use. ### Final Arrangement Points After creating the layout board, we can start creating the arrangement points. The method of adjustment is the same as the layout board—create a new arrangement point and name it according to the previous arrangement point. After creating them, arrange them separately on the corresponding layout board. Once the arrangement is complete, we need to save the layout board and arrangement points for the second time and then import them to ensure their symmetry is maintained. ### Testing the Arrangement After opening it a second time, we can test it. By clicking on one of the arrangement points, another point will automatically display light blue, indicating they are now symmetrical. When I place this board on the symmetrical layout board, another board will also automatically be placed on the symmetrical layout board. ### Using Non-Automatically Generated Layout Boards Now, let's look at non-automatically generated layout boards. Whether it is an FBX or OBJ file, we can use the layout board from another previously saved model on this model. After opening it, we can manually place these arrangement boards in the correct positions. Using the positioning ball, we can rotate and move these symmetrical arrangement boards. Once placed, considering this model may be used again, we can save it. After reopening it, it will also have arrangement points and boards. Here, we open the virtual model we just saved, press Shift + F, and see the arrangement points and boards around this model. ### Conclusion This means that if we enter a model we love that has no arrangement points or other positions, we can use a virtual model that comes with the software. They have their own set of arrangement points and boards that can be modified to match your virtual model. Of course, arrangement points and boards are not necessarily created for each model, but having them can make it more convenient for us to create clothing. When selecting an arrangement board, there will be joint names (0 and 1) at the bottom. By setting these properties, we can lock the arrangement board between these two joints. First, ensure that this model has a skeleton. After confirming, close and display the skeleton to continue adjusting the arrangement board. When selecting an arrangement board, fill in its joint name. For example, I chose the leg for the first joint name and the foot for the second. This way, the arrangement board will lock with my entire leg. If I change the position of one of the endpoints, the arrangement board's position will also change. To bind it correctly, we change joint name 1 to the foot's joint point. Now, let's change the position of the leg by pressing Shift + X to open and edit the skeleton. You can see that only the two arrangement boards tied to the virtual model joint points change according to the model's position. Press Ctrl + Z to return to the previous position, and you will see that these two arrangement points will change with each other. I recommend using these arrangement boards and skeletons to lock the virtual model joint points. See you in the next video. Bye-bye! ```
